title: Freehold vs Leasehold in Phuket: What the Difference Means
description: Freehold vs leasehold in Phuket explained: what you own, how long, the 49% foreign quota for condos and what to ask a lawyer before buying.
sub: What you actually own when you buy a condo or villa
intro: Project descriptions in Phuket keep using two terms, freehold and leasehold. They decide what you own, for how long and what rights you have. This guide explains the terms in plain language so you can prepare better questions for a lawyer.

p: Freehold is ownership with no time limit. In Thailand, foreign buyers can hold a condominium unit in their own name as freehold, provided the foreign-owned share of the building stays within the legal quota.
Currently {n_freehold} of our catalogue projects list a freehold option. Always check the ownership line on the project page and confirm it in the sale contract.

Leasehold is a long-term lease, not ownership. Under Thai law a registered lease of immovable property is limited to 30 years. Many contracts add renewal options, but renewals are a contractual promise, and you should ask a lawyer how enforceable they are in your case.
Villas on land that a foreign buyer cannot own are often sold as leasehold. Currently {n_leasehold} of our catalogue projects list a leasehold option.

sections.h2: Why villas and condos are treated differently
p: Foreign nationals generally cannot own land in Thailand, so villa projects are usually offered through a lease, a company structure or another arrangement. Condominium units are different: the Condominium Act allows foreign freehold ownership of units within a quota.
Company structures that hold land for a foreign owner draw close scrutiny from authorities. Do not accept one without independent legal advice.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you buy
ul: Is the unit freehold or leasehold, and is that written in the contract?
For leasehold: how many years, what renewal terms, and is the lease registered at the Land Department?
For freehold condos: how much of the foreign quota is already used in the building?
Who holds the title deed or chanote, and are there mortgages or charges against it?
What happens to the lease if the developer or lessor changes?

sections.h2: How this shows up in our catalogue
p: Project pages show the ownership types the developer offers. You can filter the Sale catalogue by freehold or leasehold. If a page does not state ownership, we mark it as to be confirmed with the developer rather than guessing.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal or tax advice, and rules can change. Confirm every point with a licensed Thai lawyer and the Land Department before you pay a deposit.

faq.q: Can a foreigner own a villa in Phuket?
faq.a: Foreign nationals generally cannot own land in Thailand. Villas are therefore often offered through a registered lease or other structure. Take independent legal advice on the structure before you pay.

faq.q: Is a 30-year lease the same as owning?
faq.a: No. A lease gives rights for a fixed term. Renewal clauses are contractual promises and should be reviewed by your lawyer.
